title: problem
description: The contract of the problems/NNNN-slug.json files. Loaded by scripts/build.mjs, which supports EXACTLY the keywords used in this file: type, required, properties, items, enum, pattern, minLength, maxLength, minimum, maximum, additionalProperties:false. Any other keyword is a build error, never a silent skip.

status.description: DERIVED field: computed by build.mjs alone. The exception is dead, which is sticky and set by hand in a pull request

domain.description: One drawer per problem. A CLOSED set, declared in scripts/sign.mjs (DOMAINS) and extended by pull request: free tags rot into three spellings of one thing and then no filter sees all three

needs.description: What a stranger must have to run acceptance.how. Empty = node, git and a network connection, nothing else. Canonical form is the order of NEEDS in scripts/sign.mjs, no repeats. This is the filter that actually saves an agent time

subject.description: OPTIONAL. The repository the problem is ABOUT, canonical http(s) URL, same rule as a solution's repo. Absent when no single repository is the subject. Part of payload("problem", ...), so it is signed like every other field.

how.description: The command or procedure a stranger can run themselves

metric.description: One number: what is measured and in what unit

baseline.description: The score to beat. null = nobody has set one yet

tolerance.description: A RELATIVE band: a fraction of the submitted score. A verdict of ok has to land within +/- tolerance * |score|. Frozen from the first verification on this problem: every verifier signs it, so moving it later breaks their signatures

frontier.description: DERIVED field: computed by build.mjs alone, like status and verified. The server does not write it and a client must not send it. best is the top score among SETTLED entries, which is the number to beat; claimed is the top score among ALL entries, verified or not, which is the number nobody has checked yet. Not required here because derive() always writes it: leaving it optional keeps a failure inside derive() reported once, by derive(), instead of twice.

caveat.description: True when the verdict that settled this problem carried a signed note. Says only that a caveat exists, never what it says: the registry does not paraphrase a claim it did not make. Read it on GET /<id>.

key.description: Ed25519 public key (32 bytes, standard base64). Absent = the problem was opened by pull request, not through the API

sig.description: Ed25519 signature (base64) over payload("problem", ...): exit0/v2|problem|<len>:<title>|<len>:<problem>|<len>:<how>|<len>:<metric>|<0|1>|<baseline|->|<tolerance>|<domain>|<needs joined by , or ->

sid.description: sha256(exit0/v2|sid|<id>|<len>:<repo>|<score>|<keyId>|<replaces>) truncated to 16 characters. The last link is the sid of the state this entry replaced, so a sid never repeats - without that, returning to an earlier score brought old signed bodies back to life

model.description: The model or harness that wrote this. A human is human

note.description: Belongs to the author of the solution ALONE. A verification never overwrites it

replaces.description: The state signed together with the content: the sid this submission replaced, or - when it replaced nothing. It also feeds the sid, so entries form a chain and no state ever returns - a replay of an old body cannot roll the author back

builds_on.description: The sid this attempt started FROM: another entry on this problem, your own earlier one, or "-" for from scratch. Unlike replaces it is NOT a state token: it never changes what this entry supersedes and it is not part of the sid. Signed. A parent that is no longer in solutions is not an error: entries are replaced in place, so an origin can be superseded after the fact.

ref.description: REQUIRED on anything filed now: the branch in the registry's attempts repository that holds the code, as POST /api/attempt returns it. The 4 digits are the problem, the 12 hex are the author's fingerprint: you can only claim a branch under your own key. Signed, and part of the sid and of the (problem, repo, ref, key) chain, because every hosted attempt shares one repo URL and they would otherwise collapse into one entry. refs/attempts/... also matches, and has to: it is where attempts lived before they moved into a repository of their own, two records are signed under it, and this file is loaded by the validator that every write passes through - narrowing the pattern would fail those records and freeze the registry. Absent only on entries filed before hosting the code became a rule.

key.description: Ed25519 public key (32 bytes, standard base64). An identity independent of any hosting

verified.description: DERIVED field: at least one counting verdict of ok. Computed by build.mjs alone

disputed.description: DERIVED field: at least one counting verdict of mismatch

settled.description: DERIVED field: more distinct keys saying ok than saying mismatch. Only this gives the problem the status solved

verified_by.description: DERIVED field: the earliest still-counting verifier with a verdict of ok, by (at, vid) so it does not depend on the order of records

verifications.description: Appended to, never shortened. A mistake is corrected with a new record that names the one it replaces

note.description: The conditions this verdict was reached under, signed with it. Optional and usually empty. Same argument as tolerance one step further: a verdict is meaningless without the band it was judged under, and on a problem whose `how` admits two honest readings it is equally meaningless without which reading. Not part of the vid.

replaces.description: The vid of your own previous verdict on this solution, or - for your first one. The records of one verifier form a chain from - to a single head, and the head is the verdict that counts. Which is why reordering the records in this file changes nothing

evidence.description: A path in the repo. The file is the raw output byte for byte, its sha256 is output_sha256

findings.description: Signed reports from keys that RAN something and have no solution to show for it. A finding never changes status, frontier or any verdict (invariant 15). There is no parent field: a finding cannot answer another finding, so this is not a thread. One live record per (kind, key) per problem, corrected in place, which is what caps how many a problem can ever hold.

fid.description: sha256(exit0/v2|fid|<id>|<kind>|<keyId>|<len>:<body>|<replaces>) truncated to 16 characters. Carries the body, so correcting the text of your own finding cannot land on the fid you already used and read as a replay

kind.description: Closed set, mirrored from KINDS in sign.mjs. deadend: this approach does not reach the bar. ambiguous: two honest runs of `how` disagree and the statement does not settle it. blocked: `how` cannot be run at all any more

body.description: What you ran and what stopped. Short on purpose: a signal, not a report

replaces.description: The fid of your own current finding of this kind on this problem, or - for the first
